clue.text: Irish investment in advertising has decreased

indicators.note: to invest is to put something inside, so the first word goes within the advertising piece

parts.note: ad is short for an advertisement or advertising
to get one's Irish up is to lose one's temper; bate is an old word for a rage

explanation.surface: Money from Ireland put into the advertising business has fallen off.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Irish' wants to be the nationality; it is temper, as in the idiom 'getting one's Irish up', and 'investment in' tells you where that rage goes.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: a storm that has lessened or died down is one that has decreased.

clue.text: Sportsman on the river becoming more profane

indicators.note: in a down clue, on means the first piece sits above the second

parts.note: a Blue is someone who has represented Oxford or Cambridge at sport
R is the map abbreviation for river

explanation.surface: An oarsman out on the water starts swearing more and more.
explanation.walkthrough: A Blue is a sportsman who has represented Oxford or Cambridge University, which suits the rowing picture. 'on' stacks it over R in this down entry.
explanation.definitionFit: Comparative of the adjective meaning indecent or smutty, as in coarse language or jokes.

clue.text: Volunteers to destroy natural arachnid

parts.note: TA is the Territorial Army, Britain's volunteer reserve force

indicators.note: destroying something breaks it up, so the letters of the next word are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: People offer to kill a spider found in the wild.
explanation.walkthrough: TA is the Territorial Army, Britain's part-time volunteer soldiers. 'to destroy' rearranges NATURAL into RANTULA.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: a large hairy spider, and spiders belong to that eight-legged class.

clue.text: "Treachery, Rapine, ———, and lust" (Donne)

parts.note: a quotation clue: the dash stands for the word missing from John Donne's line listing sins, to be supplied from memory

explanation.walkthrough: An old-style quotation clue with no wordplay: fill the gap in Donne's line from 'The Progress of the Soul', which runs 'Treachery, rapine, deceit, and lust'.
explanation.definitionFit: The missing word in the poet's list of vices is dishonest trickery, sitting naturally beside betrayal and plunder.

clue.text: Reason and method for making a raised footpath

parts.note: the reason for something is its cause
a method of doing something is a way of doing it

explanation.surface: Logic and a good system are needed to build an elevated walkway.
explanation.definitionFit: Dictionary sense: a path built up above wet or low ground.

clue.text: Many cats can't cha-cha, sadly, when wrestling

parts.note: C is the Roman numeral for a hundred, which crosswords call many

indicators.note: sadly suggests things have gone wrong, so the letters before it are disordered

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written, without the apostrophe
taken as written, without the hyphen

explanation.surface: Plenty of felines are hopeless at Latin dancing while they grapple with each other.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Many' is not a quantity of cats but the Roman numeral for a hundred, standing outside the jumble that 'sadly' makes of the three words before it.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: a freestyle form of grappling in which almost any hold is allowed.

clue.text: Honourable element in football supporters?

definitions.meaning: the honest, principled people in a group, described by an adjective used as a plural noun
the vertical posts that hold up the crossbar of a goal, supports rather than fans

explanation.surface: The decent, well-behaved section of a soccer crowd.
explanation.walkthrough: 'supporters' are not fans but the goalposts, which hold up the crossbar; the question mark admits the stretch.
explanation.definitionFit: Both senses share the idea of standing straight: morally principled people, and vertical goalposts.

clue.text: One of the misunderstandings in a comedy

definitions.text: One of the misunderstandings in a comedy

parts.words: One of the misunderstandings in a comedy
parts.note: points to the title of Shakespeare's farce of mistaken identity, The Comedy of ..., and asks for just one of the mistakes

explanation.surface: A single mix-up in a funny play.
explanation.walkthrough: The comedy is Shakespeare's The Comedy of Errors, so one of its misunderstandings is the singular of the title's last word.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym for a mistake, with a nod to the Shakespeare title that pluralises it.

clue.text: Reptile has a drink coming up a hill

indicators.note: in a down clue, coming up means the drink is written from bottom to top

parts.note: a gill is a quarter-pint measure of drink
a tor is a rocky hill, as on Dartmoor

explanation.surface: A lizard climbs a slope with a beverage.
explanation.walkthrough: 'coming up' turns GILL, an old British quarter-pint measure, into LLIG. A tor is a rocky hill, as on Dartmoor in south-west England.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: a large scaly cold-blooded animal of American swamps.

clue.text: Labour trick almost confused one promoting revolution

indicators.note: confused means muddled, so the letters before it are mixed up

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: almost means the word before it falls just short, losing its final letter

parts.note: taken as written before it loses its last letter

explanation.surface: A left-wing ruse nearly baffles an agitator stirring up revolt.
explanation.walkthrough: 'almost' cuts TRICK to TRIC, and 'confused' rearranges LABOUR TRIC. The revolution is the turning of machinery, not an uprising.
explanation.definitionFit: Cryptic sense: oil or an oiler helps wheels and shafts turn smoothly.

clue.text: A part in "Bread", say

indicators.note: say means the bread word is spoken rather than spelt

parts.note: a roll is a small individual loaf of bread

explanation.surface: An actor lands a character in the television sitcom Bread.
explanation.walkthrough: Bread was a 1980s BBC sitcom, which makes the surface about casting; here it is simply a bread roll, heard as 'say' asks.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: an actor's character in a play or show.

clue.text: This trade mark is hard to display

parts.note: a brand is a maker's trade mark
taken as written
H is the pencil-grade abbreviation for hard

explanation.surface: A company logo proves difficult to show off.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: to wave something about so as to show it off.

clue.text: It supplies cars to shooting men covered by guarantee

indicators.note: what is covered lies inside its cover, so the shooting men sit within the guarantee

parts.note: a gage is a pledge or security given as a guarantee
RA is the Royal Artillery, the British Army's gunners

explanation.surface: A dealer provides vehicles under warranty to a party of marksmen.
explanation.walkthrough: The 'shooting men' are the Royal Artillery, the British Army's gunners, abbreviated RA. 'covered by' puts them inside GAGE, a pledge.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: a motor dealership that sells vehicles.

clue.text: The arm, they say, of the ladies' man

indicators.note: they say means the weapon's name is heard, not read

parts.note: an arm is a weapon, and a bow is the archer's weapon

explanation.surface: People gossip about the limb of a womaniser.
explanation.walkthrough: 'arm' is a weapon, not a limb: the archer's BOW, heard as 'they say' asks.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: a dandy or male admirer who courts women.

clue.text: Eurasian rose in a gentle potpourri

indicators.note: a potpourri is a mixture, so the words before it are mixed together

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A flower from the East scents a mild bowl of dried petals.
explanation.walkthrough: 'potpourri', a mixture, rearranges IN A GENTLE. The 'in' looks like a link word but is needed as fodder.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: the sweet-briar, a wild species native to Europe and western Asia.

clue.text: Thoroughly wet god detailed to accompany a goddess

indicators.note: read as de-tailed, it means the god loses his final letter

parts.note: Saturn is the Roman god of agriculture
Ate is the Greek goddess of mischief and ruin

explanation.surface: A drenched deity is assigned to escort a female divinity.
explanation.walkthrough: 'detailed' must be read as de-tailed: SATURN loses its last letter, giving SATUR. Ate is the Greek goddess of mischief.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym as a verb: to soak something completely.

clue.text: See parson about taking back pictures — it needs muscle

indicators.note: about means the parson goes round the outside of the other piece

parts.note: a rector is a parish clergyman

indicators.note: taking back means the pictures are written the other way round

parts.note: pictures such as paintings are art

explanation.surface: Visit the vicar about returning the paintings, which takes some strength.
explanation.walkthrough: 'See' is just an instruction to the solver. 'taking back' applies only to the pictures, and 'about' then wraps the clergyman round them.
explanation.definitionFit: Cryptic sense: a surgeon's instrument for holding back tissue such as muscle, and also the name of a muscle that draws a part in.

clue.text: Not material for a naval man's treatise

parts.note: AB is an able-bodied seaman, and the possessive adds the S
a tract is a short treatise, often religious

explanation.surface: This is unsuitable content for a sailor's learned essay.
explanation.walkthrough: AB is an able-bodied seaman, and here the possessive S is kept as a letter. 'material' means physical, not subject matter.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: existing as an idea rather than as a physical thing.

clue.text: Man gets food and support in the Palace

parts.note: Al is a man's name
ham is a food
a bra is a supporting garment

explanation.surface: A fellow is given his meals and financial backing at the royal residence.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: the famous Moorish fortress-residence in Granada, Spain.

clue.text: Twister has no trouble with rent

indicators.note: has no means the twister loses the letters of the trouble word

parts.note: a twister is an informal name for a tornado
ado is fuss or trouble

explanation.surface: A swindler finds paying the landlord no bother at all.
explanation.walkthrough: 'has no' takes ADO out of TORNADO. 'rent' is not a payment but the past participle of rend.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: ripped apart, the past participle of rend.

clue.text: Just the tool for a puzzle

definitions.meaning: a power saw with a fine blade for cutting curves
a picture cut into interlocking pieces to be put back together

explanation.surface: Exactly the right implement for solving a brain-teaser.
explanation.definitionFit: Both senses: a fine-bladed saw for cutting curves, and the picture game originally cut with one.

clue.text: A man for Falstaff, say

definitions.meaning: a man is a chess piece, and this is one of them
Shakespeare's Sir John Falstaff holds this rank, as his title Sir shows

explanation.surface: An actor suited to playing Shakespeare's fat rogue, for instance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'man' is a chess piece. Falstaff is Sir John Falstaff in Shakespeare, so he is an example of the rank.
explanation.definitionFit: Both senses: a chess piece, and the rank of someone titled Sir.

clue.text: Proceeding — not yet knocked down

definitions.meaning: moving along or making one's way
the auctioneer's cry before the hammer falls and the lot is sold

explanation.surface: Carrying on walking, still on one's feet.
explanation.walkthrough: An auctioneer knocks a lot down with the hammer; before that he calls this word twice, then 'gone'.
explanation.definitionFit: Both senses: moving onward, and the auctioneer's call while a lot is still unsold.

clue.text: National ball

definitions.meaning: a dated term for a citizen of an Asian country
in cricket, a left-arm wrist-spinner's delivery that turns in to a right-hander

explanation.definitionFit: Both senses: a dated word for a citizen of an Asian country, and a kind of cricket delivery.

clue.text: Concur in a Green Party project

indicators.note: in says the answer lies inside the run of words that follows

explanation.surface: Go along with an environmentalist political scheme.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' points to consecutive letters at the start of 'a Green Party project'.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: to be of the same opinion.

clue.text: Two soldiers in a film

indicators.note: two means the soldier's abbreviation is written twice over

parts.note: a GI is an American soldier

explanation.surface: A pair of servicemen appear in a movie.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: the 1958 MGM musical starring Leslie Caron.

clue.text: Coppers are after Bill, a politician, implying blame

indicators.note: are after means the coppers follow the bill in the answer

parts.note: AC is short for account, a bill
Cu is the chemical symbol for copper, so more than one gives CUS
a Tory is a member of Britain's Conservative Party

explanation.surface: The police are chasing William, an MP, and hinting that he is guilty.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Coppers' are not police but the metal, Cu, in the plural; 'are after' puts them behind AC, an account. A Tory is a British Conservative.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: suggesting that someone is at fault.

clue.text: Become more intense with female in crew? On the contrary

indicators.note: in signals one piece inside the other, and the words On the contrary swap which goes inside

parts.note: a hen is a female bird
an eight is a rowing crew of eight oarsmen

explanation.surface: Things hot up when a woman joins the boat's team, or perhaps the opposite.
explanation.walkthrough: 'female in crew' as written gives nothing; 'On the contrary' flips it, so the rowing crew goes inside the female bird.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: to increase in strength or degree.

clue.text: Retreat after fighting the governor

indicators.note: after means the retreat follows the fighting in the answer

parts.note: war is fighting
a den is a private retreat or hideaway

explanation.surface: The army falls back once it has battled the colonial ruler.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Retreat' is a noun, a hideaway, not a military withdrawal; 'after' places it behind WAR.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: the head of a prison or an Oxford college.
